title: Codex CLI da OpenAI como backend alternativo completo ao Claude (selecionavel no cam config)
description: OBJETIVO: o Codex CLI da OpenAI (comando `codex`) como alternativa COMPLETA ao `claude`: o harness inteiro roda em OU claude (+ seus modelos) OU codex (+ seus modelos), escolhido no menu de config. DEPENDE de CAM-53 (o seletor de backend + os modelos vivem la); planejar/implementar CAM-53 antes. Exige abstrair o backend atras de uma interface cobrindo: (a) invocacao do worker (claude --agent X --session-id <uuid> '<prompt>' vs a invocacao do codex); (b) deteccao de conclusao (o polling do sentinel CAM_*_STATUS / <review> no capture-pane vs o equivalente no codex); (c) modelo de sessao/agente (o codex tem seu proprio modelo de agent-definition e de resume de sessao, diferente do --agent + --session-id do claude); (d) launch da persona do orquestrador (wrapper bash do bounded-respawn). SPIKE DE DESIGN PRIMEIRO (antes de codar): mapear a CLI do codex (invocacao, sessao, output/sentinel, config de modelo/agent), identificar o que NAO mapeia pro modelo do cam, e decidir a fronteira da abstracao (uma interface BackendAdapter com claude e codex como implementacoes). ESCOPO: abstracao BackendAdapter no worker-spawn + supervisor + run.ts; adapter do codex; wiring de config (de CAM-53); os prompts dos agentes (subagent-*.md) podem precisar de forma codex-compativel; os modelos do codex sao configuraveis no menu. RELACIONA: CAM-53 (pre-req), CAM-42 (modelo de worker TUI + sentinel que precisa ser re-implementado pro codex), regra no-claude-p (revisitar o equivalente no codex). ACEITE: com backend=codex no config, `cam run`/plan/next/review/ship funcionam ponta-a-ponta no codex; backend=claude inalterado; spike de design documentado antes da implementacao; typecheck; tests.

spec.scope: Wire the OpenAI Codex CLI (codex) as an LLM backend that is selectable PER-SUBAGENT: claude and codex can each be used alone OR MIXED in one run -- every worker phase (implementer, planner, auditor, reviewer) is independently configured claude|codex via the config 'wiring'. This mirrors the existing PER-PHASE model config (models.ts DEFAULTS / readPhaseModel), not a single global switch. DESIGN SPIKE FIRST (the issue demands it): the first deliverable is an ADR defining a BackendAdapter abstraction seam and resolving the six claude/codex mismatches; codex dispatch code lands only after the spike ADR. CAM-53 shipped config plumbing (a single top-level backend string default claude, ConfigScreen option labeled 'wired in CAM-54') + the runtime guard (spawn-resolution.ts:60 CODEX_GUARD_NOTICE) -- this issue turns the single-key backend into a per-phase setting and replaces the guard's not-yet-wired behavior with real dispatch. Abstraction boundary = the report/sentinel/JSON contract (CAM_*_STATUS lines, <review> tags, worker-report.json/review-report.json), whose parsing is already backend-agnostic (report-parse.ts, ADR-0038); this boundary is what makes a MIXED run work -- every actor, whatever its backend, emits the identical contract. The BackendAdapter (resolved PER-ACTOR at each worker dispatch) encapsulates spawn argv, completion detection, session/transcript model, agent-prompt injection, permission/sandbox+env, and model-id namespace. Codex runs as a TUI pane (operator steer) mirroring the claude worker model. IN SCOPE: spike ADR + BackendAdapter seam + per-phase backend config + codex wired end-to-end for the worker actors, alone or mixed with claude. FOLLOW-UPS (out, separate issues): orchestrator-persona (run.ts bounded-respawn wrapper), retry launcher, auth-preflight codex parity. OUT OF SCOPE entirely: ship (deterministic zero-LLM, ship-runner.ts:36). Epic-scale: expect heavy slicing.
acceptanceCriteria: A design-spike ADR is written FIRST, defining the BackendAdapter abstraction seam and resolving the six claude/codex mismatches (seam; session/transcript + budget-recycle; completion-detection; agent-prompt injection; permission/sandbox+env; model-id namespace); it lands before any codex dispatch code.

A BackendAdapter abstraction fronts the worker spawn-argv builders (worker-argv.ts, plan-argv.ts, review.ts) and their loop.ts/review.ts call sites, resolved PER-ACTOR; claude is refactored into an adapter with NO behavior change (existing claude path + tests stay green).

Backend is configurable PER-SUBAGENT, not a single global key: each worker phase (implementer, planner, auditor, reviewer) independently selects claude or codex and the selections are mixable in one run; a per-phase backend accessor is added mirroring readPhaseModel(phase), and ConfigScreen wires each subagent's backend.

codex is wired as a real backend for the worker actors running as TUI panes emitting the shared CAM_*_STATUS / <review> / worker-report.json / review-report.json contract; a MIXED run (e.g. implementer=codex, reviewer=claude) interoperates because every actor emits the identical contract, and selecting codex for a phase dispatches codex (the spawn-resolution not-yet-wired notice is replaced by real dispatch).
The context-budget/recycle backstop behaves correctly for a codex worker per the spike's decision (a codex transcript equivalent OR documented graceful degradation), never silently broken.

codex model ids populate the per-phase model config for phases whose backend=codex (backend-conditional ConfigScreen + models.ts) without breaking the claude tier-alias path for phases that stay claude.
Orchestrator-persona, retry launcher, and auth-preflight codex parity are OUT of scope (tracked as follow-ups); ship stays zero-LLM and unaffected.

typecheck passes, check:all is green, the claude backend path is unchanged (all existing tests pass), and new tests cover the BackendAdapter seam, per-phase backend resolution, the codex argv/adapter, and a mixed-backend scenario.
gotchas: PER-SUBAGENT mixing is the core requirement: backend is per-phase (implementer/planner/auditor/reviewer each claude|codex, mixable), NOT a single global switch; model it on the existing per-phase model config (models.ts DEFAULTS :62-70, readPhaseModel :110-125), and upgrade the single-key readBackend (models.ts:171-191) to a per-phase accessor.
'backend' is overloaded: the issue_system backend (local/github/linear) is a DIFFERENT concept; CAM-53/54 mean the LLM backend (claude/codex) in src/config/models.ts + src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx.

CAM-53 shipped only config plumbing + a guard, NO abstraction: readBackend (models.ts:171-191), DEFAULTS backend:'claude' (:62-70), ConfigScreen BACKEND_OPTIONS codex labeled 'wired in CAM-54' (:131-135), CODEX_GUARD_NOTICE (spawn-resolution.ts:60, informational, still spawns claude).

Every spawn path hardcodes claude: worker-argv.ts:177-192 (implementer), plan-argv.ts:85-99 (planner) + :146-160 (auditor), review.ts:119-133 (reviewer), run.ts:252-308/:267 (orchestrator persona), claude.ts (cam claude wrapper), run-auth-preflight.ts:81, retry/launcher.ts:81-86.

The report/sentinel/JSON contract is the portable boundary and the enabler of MIXED runs: parsing is backend-agnostic (report-parse.ts, ADR-0038); codex agents must be prompted to emit the same CAM_*_STATUS lines / <review> tags / JSON reports so a codex worker and a claude worker are interchangeable in one run.
ship is deterministic zero-LLM (ship-runner.ts:36, ADR-0009) -- no codex adapter needed there.

RISKIEST sub-area: the context-budget/recycle backstop hard-couples to claude's transcript (transcript/usage.ts:232-234, orch-budget.ts, orch-recycle-watch.ts) + the --session-id lowercase-uuid uuidgen respawn dance (run.ts:281-285); codex's session/transcript model differs -- the spike decides a codex equivalent or graceful degradation. (Most of this lives in the orchestrator-persona path, a follow-up, but codex worker completion detection is in scope.)

--agent <name> -> .claude/agents/*.md (ADR-0020; the agent body IS the system prompt) has no codex analog; the spike defines codex's prompt-injection path and whether codex-shaped agent files are needed.

--permission-mode bypassPermissions must NEVER be a cam CLI flag (test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts); codex has its own sandbox/approval model + different nesting/auth env vars vs the CLAUDE* env-strip (worker-argv.ts:82-102).
No MCP surface exists (grep clean) and no trust-prompt handling exists (sidestepped by bypassPermissions) -- nothing to port there.
CAM-42's no-claude-p rule (subscription; TUI panes + sentinel polling, not headless -p) needs a codex equivalent decision in the spike.
Model tier aliases are claude-only (ADR-0034); codex ids are a different namespace populating the same per-phase slots for codex phases.
No ADR/CONTEXT entry for codex or the backend-split exists yet; the spike creates the first.
domainTerms: LLM backend: the claude-vs-codex choice per worker phase (src/config/models.ts), distinct from the issue_system backend (local/github/linear).

per-subagent backend wiring: the config that assigns each worker phase (implementer/planner/auditor/reviewer) its own backend (claude|codex), mixable in a single run, mirroring the per-phase model config.

BackendAdapter: the per-actor abstraction seam fronting spawn argv, completion detection, session/transcript model, agent-prompt injection, permission/sandbox+env, and model-id namespace for a given LLM backend.
design spike: the issue's mandated first deliverable -- a design ADR resolving the claude/codex mismatches before any codex dispatch code.

report/sentinel contract: the backend-agnostic completion+result boundary (CAM_*_STATUS lines, <review> tags, worker-report.json/review-report.json) parsed by report-parse.ts (ADR-0038); the enabler of mixed-backend runs.
context-budget/recycle backstop: the claude-transcript-driven subsystem (orch-budget.ts, orch-recycle-watch.ts) that recycles the orchestrator near context exhaustion; claude-shaped today.
